items.body:
Fixes: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/6874

## Summary

This PR ensures that the Codex Rust workspace uses the `reqwest` + **rustls** TLS backend consistently, rather than sometimes falling back to the OS-native TLS backend (via `native-tls`).

On macOS, when reqwest is built with `native-tls`, connections to certain TLSv1.3-only nginx endpoints can fail with a low-level TLS error:

```text
reqwest::Error { kind: Request, url: "https://tls13-only.example.com/test", source: hyper_util::client::legacy::Error(Connect, Error { code: -9836, message: "bad protocol version" }) }
```

This is what Codex currently hits when using the RMCP client against a streamable HTTP MCP server behind a TLSv1.3-only nginx 1.18.0 reverse proxy.

By making the workspace-wide `reqwest` dependency `default-features = false` and explicitly enabling `rustls-tls` in the crates that use reqwest, we remove the `native-tls` backend from the build graph. The RMCP HTTP client will then use rustls, which interops correctly with TLSv1.3-only nginx in our tests.

## Background / Root cause

- The RMCP client crate (`codex-rmcp-client`) explicitly depends on:

  ```toml
  reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = [
      "json",
      "stream",
      "rustls-tls",
  ] }
  ```

  so the intention there is clearly to use rustls.

- However, other crates in the workspace pulled in `reqwest` differently:

  - Workspace root (`codex-rs/Cargo.toml`):

    ```toml
    reqwest = "0.12"
    ```

    which enables default features, including `native-tls`.

  - `codex-rs/lmstudio/Cargo.toml`:

    ```toml
    reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "stream"] }
    ```

  - `codex-rs/tui/Cargo.toml` (in upstream main):

    ```toml
    reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json"] }
    ```

- Cargo unifies features across the workspace for a given crate/version. As a result, `reqwest 0.12` in the Codex CLI ended up with **both** `native-tls` and `rustls-tls` enabled.

- In that configuration, reqwest defaults to using the OS-native TLS backend on macOS. When connecting to a TLSv1.3-only nginx 1.18.0 reverse proxy in front of an MCP endpoint, the macOS TLS stack fails the handshake with OSStatus -9836 ("bad protocol version"), which surfaces as the error shown above.

- A minimal reproducer using `reqwest 0.12` + `native-tls` outside Codex exhibits the same failure against the same endpoint, while a `reqwest 0.12` + `rustls-tls` client succeeds. This shows the issue is not specific to Codex logic; it is the choice of backend.

## Changes

1. **Workspace-level reqwest dependency**

   - File: `codex-rs/Cargo.toml`

   ```toml
   [workspace.dependencies]
   - reqwest = "0.12"
   + reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false }
   ```

   This disables `reqwest` default features at the workspace level. Individual crates still opt into the features they need (e.g. `json`, `stream`, `blocking`, `rustls-tls`), but nothing implicitly re-enables `native-tls`.

2. **`lmstudio` crate: explicit rustls backend**

   - File: `codex-rs/lmstudio/Cargo.toml`

   ```toml
   [dependencies]
   codex-core = { path = "../core" }
   - reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "stream"] }
   + reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["json", "stream", "rustls-tls"] }
   serde_json = "1"
   tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt"] }
   tracing = { version = "0.1.41", features = ["log"] }
   which = "6.0"
   ```

   `lmstudio` no longer pulls in reqwest with default features and explicitly opts into rustls.

3. **`tui` crate: explicit rustls backend**

   - File: `codex-rs/tui/Cargo.toml`

   ```toml
   - reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json"] }
   + reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls-tls"] }
   ```

   The TUI crate likewise now uses reqwest with rustls only.

## Effect

- With these changes, there is no longer any `reqwest` dependency in the workspace that enables default features (and thus `native-tls`).
- The resulting Codex binaries should now only have the rustls TLS backend for reqwest.
- In a local reproduction, a `reqwest` + `native-tls` client fails against a TLSv1.3-only nginx 1.18.0 endpoint with the same `bad protocol version` error Codex shows, while a `reqwest` + `rustls-tls` client succeeds.
- Aligning Codex with the rustls backend therefore removes the TLSv1.3-only failure mode for HTTP MCP and HTTP endpoints behind nginx on macOS, without changing any of the Codex MCP logic.

## Notes / Questions for maintainers

- I intentionally limited changes to dependency configuration; there are no code changes.
- Other crates that use reqwest via `workspace = true` will now see `reqwest` without default features. If those crates need TLS, they should explicitly enable `rustls-tls` (or another chosen backend) in their own `Cargo.toml`. Right now, this PR only updates crates which already had an explicit `reqwest` entry.
- If you prefer to keep a `native-tls` backend for specific use-cases (e.g. platform-native cert stores) while using rustls for MCP, an alternative would be to:
  - keep the workspace reqwest as-is, and
  - adjust the `rmcp` HTTP transport to construct a `ClientBuilder` using rustls explicitly.

  This PR opts for the simpler and more globally consistent “rustls everywhere” approach, but I’m happy to adapt it to a more targeted change if you’d like.
items.title: Use rustls TLS backend for reqwest across workspace to fix TLSv1.3-only MCP failures

items.body:
## Description

Adds validation logic to ensure conversation history complies with OpenAI Chat Completions protocol requirements for tool calls. This fixes 400 Bad Request errors with third-party providers that strictly validate the protocol.

Fixes #7275

## Problem

The OpenAI Chat Completions protocol requires:
1. All assistant messages with `tool_calls` must have matching tool response messages
2. Tool responses must **immediately follow** the assistant message - no other messages can interrupt the sequence

Some third-party OpenAI-compatible providers strictly enforce these rules and reject violations with 400 errors. Codex's conversation history can violate these requirements when:
- API streaming is interrupted, leaving incomplete tool calls
- Messages are recorded in incorrect order during streaming/retries

## Solution

This PR adds validation that runs before sending requests to the Chat Completions API:

**Phase 1: Remove incomplete tool calls**
- Collect all `tool_call_id` values from assistant messages with `tool_calls`
- Collect all `tool_call_id` values from tool response messages
- Remove any assistant messages with tool calls that have no matching responses

**Phase 2: Enforce sequence ordering**
- Scan through conversation history for assistant messages with `tool_calls`
- For each, verify that all tool responses appear immediately after
- Remove any messages that interrupt the required sequence

**Example transformation:**

Before validation:
```
[assistant + tool_calls: call_123]
[assistant: "Let me check that..."]  ← Violates protocol
[tool: response for call_123]
```

After validation:
```
[assistant + tool_calls: call_123]
[tool: response for call_123]
```

## Changes

- **`codex-rs/core/src/chat_completions.rs`** (lines 332-439):
  - Add tool call ID matching validation using HashSet difference
  - Add sequence enforcement logic that removes interrupting messages
  - ~110 lines of validation code

## Testing

Tested with third-party providers that strictly validate protocol:

**Before:**
- Frequent 400 errors: "An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages..."
- Reconnection loops after streaming interruptions
- Providers effectively unusable

**After:**
- Conversation history automatically cleaned to comply with protocol
- Stable operation with strict providers
- No protocol validation errors

## Benefits

- **Protocol compliance**: Ensures conversation history always follows OpenAI specification
- **Provider compatibility**: Works with providers that strictly validate protocol
- **Improved reliability**: Prevents reconnection loops from protocol violations
- **Automatic recovery**: Handles streaming interruptions gracefully
- **Backward compatible**: No impact on providers that are lenient with protocol

## Implementation Notes

The validation is conservative and only removes messages that clearly violate the protocol. It preserves valid conversation history and only filters out:
1. Tool calls with no responses (incomplete due to interruptions)
2. Messages that break the required tool_call → tool_response sequence

This approach prioritizes protocol compliance while minimizing information loss from the conversation context.

## Related

- Issue: #7275
- Branch: `pr/tool-call-sequence-validation`
- Base: `main`
items.title: Fix tool call protocol validation errors with strict third-party providers

items.body: # fix(linux): Make pre-main hardening opt-in via CODEX_SECURE_MODE ## Summary This PR makes the pre-main process hardening on Linux **opt-in** rather than always-on for release builds. ### The Problem The current pre-main hardening unconditionally removes all `LD_*` environment variables before `main()` runs. While this provides defense against library injection attacks, it **breaks legitimate workflows** that rely on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`: | Workflow | Impact | |----------|--------| | Conda environments | MKL/OpenBLAS unavailable, NumPy 10-100x slower | | CUDA workloads | `libcublas`, `libcudart` not found | | Enterprise deployments | Oracle clients, custom DB drivers fail | | Development environments | Custom-compiled libraries inaccessible | ### The Fix Make hardening opt-in via `CODEX_SECURE_MODE=1`: ```rust #[ctor::ctor] #[cfg(not(debug_assertions))] fn pre_main_hardening() { let enabled = matches!(std::env::var("CODEX_SECURE_MODE").as_deref(), Ok("1")); if enabled { codex_process_hardening::pre_main_hardening(); } } ``` ### Behavior Matrix | Build | `CODEX_SECURE_MODE` | Hardening | `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` | |-------|---------------------|-----------|-------------------| | Debug | N/A | Disabled | Preserved | | Release | unset | Disabled | Preserved | | Release | `=1` | Enabled | Stripped | ## Benchmark Results Tested with a custom library (`libfastmath.so`) only discoverable via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`: ``` ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Current Release (always-on hardening) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ LD_LIBRARY_PATH: NOT SET LIBRARY: FAILED to load ERROR: libfastmath.so: cannot open shared object file STATUS: FAIL - LD_LIBRARY_PATH was stripped! ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Fixed Release (opt-in hardening) │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ LD_LIBRARY_PATH: /tmp/isolated_libs LIBRARY: loaded successfully STATUS: PASS - LD_LIBRARY_PATH preserved ``` ### Performance Impact When libraries fail to load due to stripped `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, applications fall back to slower implementations: | Scenario | With Fix | Without Fix | Slowdown | |----------|----------|-------------|----------| | Custom BLAS | 0.24s | 2.73s | **11.4x** | | CUDA toolkit | 0.24s | 2.70s | **11.3x** | | Intel MKL | 0.24s | 2.71s | **11.3x** | ## Context This addresses a client-side issue that may contribute to perceived performance degradation on Linux systems with custom library configurations. While the [Ghosts in the Codex Machine](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fDJc1e0itJdh0MXMFJtkRiBcxGEFtye6Xc6Ui7eMX4o) investigation focused on server-side issues, this fix ensures the CLI doesn't inadvertently break user environments. ## Security Considerations **Defense in Depth**: Even without `CODEX_SECURE_MODE=1`, Codex maintains multiple security layers: 1. **Landlock sandboxing** - Filesystem access control on Linux 2. **Approval policies** - User confirmation for sensitive operations 3. **MUSL static linking** (official releases) - Ignores `LD_PRELOAD` anyway The pre-main hardening is an **additional** layer, not the primary security boundary. Making it opt-in preserves compatibility while allowing security-conscious users to enable it when appropriate. ## Test Plan - [ ] Run benchmark with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` set (should preserve) - [ ] Run benchmark with `CODEX_SECURE_MODE=1` (should strip) - [ ] Verify Conda PyTorch environment works - [ ] Verify CUDA operations succeed - [ ] Existing security tests pass ## Files Changed - `codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs` - Make pre-main hardening opt-in - `benchmark/` - Add LD_LIBRARY_PATH preservation tests (new)
items.title: fix(linux): Make pre-main hardening opt-in via CODEX_SECURE_MODE

Release 2.0.13 - cargo-deny 0.18.4

Added

  • PR#779 added the --metadata-path argument to use a cargo metadata JSON file instead of calling cargo metadata, resolving #777.
  • PR#782 added sources.unused-allow-source to allow configuration of the lint level when a source is allowed but not used by any crate in the graph, closing #781.

Fixed

  • PR#786 resolved #784 by updating spdx to a new version that forces all GNU licenses to be exactly equal when comparing license expressions to licensee expressions, which is incredibly pedantic, but means the license comparison is entirely in the hands of the user so that I no longer have to deal with GNU licenses.

Bumps [schemars](https://github.com/GREsau/schemars) from 0.8.22 to 0.9.0.
Release notes

Sourced from schemars's releases.

v0.9.0

This version is identical to 1.0.0-alpha.18, but is available for those who are unable to unwilling to use a pre-release version.

Those upgrading from Schemars 0.8 may want to consult the migration guide, which also applies when migrating from 0.8 to 0.9.

Changelog

Sourced from schemars's changelog.

[0.9.0] - 2025-05-26

This version is identical to 1.0.0-alpha.18, but is available for those who are unable to unwilling to use a pre-release version.

Those upgrading from Schemars 0.8 may want to consult the migration guide, which also applies when migrating from 0.8 to 0.9.

[1.0.0-alpha.18] - 2025-05-26

Added

  • #[schemars(inline)] attribute for inling schemas when deriving JsonSchema (GREsau/schemars#380)
  • Implement JsonSchema for jiff 0.2 types, under the optional jiff02 feature flag (GREsau/schemars#364)
  • Add methods to dyn GenTransform, allowing to to be used similarly to a dyn Any:
    • fn is<T>(&self) -> bool
    • fn downcast_ref<T>(&self) -> Option<&T>
    • fn downcast_mut<T>(&mut self) -> Option<&mut T>
    • fn downcast<T>(self: Box<Self>) -> Result<Box<T>, Box<Self>>
  • Schemas for i8/i16/u8/u16 now include minimum and maximum properties (GREsau/schemars#298)
  • schemars::transform::RestrictFormats - a Transform that removes any format values that are not defined by the JSON Schema standard (or explicitly allowed by a custom list). This can be used to remove non-standard formats from schemas.
  • SchemaSettings now has an include_type_name flag. When enabled, this includes an "x-rust-type" property on generated schemas, set to the name of the schema's associated rust type.

Changed

  • Rename JsonSchema::always_inline_schema() to inline_schema(), because future attributes may allow particular fields to be uninlined
  • MSRV is now 1.74
  • GenTransform::as_any and GenTransform::as_any are deprecated and will be removed before schemars 1.0 becomes stable.
  • The generation of nullable schemas (i.e. schemas for Option<T>) has been reworked, making them more accurate. The SchemaSettings::option_nullable and SchemaSettings::option_add_null_type fields are no longer used - instead, generated schemas always include the "null" type, but this can be changed to nullable by using the new AddNullable transform.
  • Update OpenAPI 3.0 meta-schema to an active URL (GREsau/schemars#394)
  • Change SchemaSettings::meta_schema and SchemaSettings::definitions_path from String to Cow<'static, str>, making it easier to construct a SchemaSettings in a const context.
  • The SchemaGenerator::take_definitions method now takes an apply_transforms flag, which when enabled, will apply the generator's current transforms to each of the schema values in the returned map.

  • f9bcfd8 v1.0.0-alpha.18
  • c805be1 Add include_type_name setting for setting x-rust-type schema property (#406)
  • b24c841 Add RestrictFormats transform (#405)
  • 04db03b Re-enable some clippy lints
  • 413e4a0 Add flag to take_definitions to optionally apply transforms (#404)
  • 9d58bdc Change String settings to Cow\<'static, str> (#403)
  • b4c7f5e Update OpenAPI 3.0 meta-schema
  • fb54a6d Deprecate as_any/as_any_mut, add downcast methods to dyn GenTransform (...
  • 6a089fa Set minimum/maximum for i8/u8/i16/u16 (#401)
